title: feat(cli)!: a declared multi-replica os start on the redis cluster driver refuses to boot without OS_AUTH_SECRET, instead of minting its own sign-in secret
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9EaMu5Cnk8LQVwSLuDZCP1u)_

Fixes #31600

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — measured: on base `fc4c3072` an `os start` declaring several replicas (`OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true`) over the redis cluster driver, with `OS_SECRET_KEY` set and no `OS_AUTH_SECRET`, booted (redis cluster driver and redis cache adapter registered, `Press Ctrl+C to stop`) and generated `{home}/auth-secret`; on head the same start exits 1 on the refusal line and generates nothing.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here — `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (the `--auth-secret` row and the Authentication paragraph) and `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` (the `OS_AUTH_SECRET` row) no longer say `os start` always generates a secret; `skills/**` says nothing about `os start` generating one on a multi-replica deployment (its only `OS_AUTH_SECRET` text is the image's durability refusal, unchanged).

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：`os start` 在"声明多副本（`OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` 或 `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS`>1）且集群驱动是 Redis"时，如果没设 `OS_AUTH_SECRET`，不再自己生成登录密钥，而是直接拒绝启动，打印一行：缺哪个变量、为什么、怎么生成（`openssl rand -hex 32`），所有副本设同一个值。
- **为什么改**：以前每个副本各自生成一份密钥存在自己的盘上，r1 签发的登录 cookie 到 r3 就失效（卡上的冒烟现象，这里实测复现：两副本密钥不同，r2 不认 r1 的 cookie；密钥相同则两边都认）。
- **风险与回滚**：单节点（没声明多副本）照旧自动生成并复用 `{home}/auth-secret`，任何驱动都一样；声明多副本但驱动不是 Redis 的维持原样（R3：两个条件同时成立才生效）。会被拒绝的只有"多副本 + Redis + 没设密钥"这一种配置，修法就是设密钥。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：① `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` 生成密钥之前新加的那一段判断与 `declaresReplicasSharingState`；② 同文件的拒绝文案 `MULTI_REPLICA_AUTH_SECRET_REFUSAL`；③ `packages/cli/test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts` 新增的三条真实 `os start` 用例。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/commands/start-deployment-durability.test.ts test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts`（需先 build CLI），预期 35 passed：其中多副本 + Redis + 无密钥的 `os start` 退出码 1、输出那一行、家目录里没有 `auth-secret`。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**`os start` refuses to generate a sign-in secret for a declared multi-replica deployment on the redis cluster driver.** Where the operator set no secret (`--auth-secret`, `OS_AUTH_SECRET` or its legacy names unset or blank), `os start` now asks, before it generates anything, whether the deployment runs replicas that share state. If it does, it exits 1 on one line, in the data key refusal's shape:

```text
[auth] Refusing to start: several replicas are declared (OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE / OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS>1) over the redis cluster driver, but OS_AUTH_SECRET is not set — each replica would mint its own sign-in secret, and a session signed on one would be refused on the others. Fix: generate one and set the same value on every replica, e.g. OS_AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
```

The line names the variable and never a value. The refusal writes no secret, so a replica that hits it leaves nothing on its volume.

**Where it lives, measured in step 0.** The only place a sign-in secret is generated is `os start` itself (`readOrCreateAuthSecret`, `{home}/auth-secret`; the image's home is the `/data/auth-secret` of the card). `os serve` never generates one outside development: plugin-auth refuses a production boot without `OS_AUTH_SECRET`. The data key's missing-key refusal lives in the `serve` child (`LocalCryptoProvider`), and `os start` already declines to opt that key into self-minting when `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` is set. The secret is generated in the parent before the child starts, so the refusal belongs in the parent, at the same point as the image's durability check, which it follows.

**The predicate is not a second copy.** It is the rule every multi-replica change keeps (cloud#3814 R3): replicas declared (`declaresMultiNode`, the split-brain guard's reader) AND the `redis` cluster driver. PR #31624 applies it in `planCacheAdapter` to the registered cluster service's driver; its one pre-boot form already exists as `sharesCloudBindingCredential(env, OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER)` in `@objectstack/cloud-connection` (it trims the driver the way the `serve` child does before composing the cluster service). `os start` asks that function, through a lazy import of a package the CLI already declares. A first attempt declared `@objectstack/service-cluster` on the CLI to import `declaresMultiNode` directly; `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` refuses that, because cluster packages ship with the host app and the open-core CLI takes no static dependency on them, so the dependency was dropped.

**Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (the `--auth-secret` row and the Authentication paragraph) and `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` (the `OS_AUTH_SECRET` row) said `os start` always generates a secret; they now name the one topology where it refuses instead.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/src/commands/start-deployment-durability.test.ts`, new top-level `describe`: the decision on real environments — refused for `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=3` and for `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` (with a padded `' redis '`) over redis; CONTROL single node (no declaration, redis alone, replicas `1`) not refused; CONTROL replicas declared over `memory` or no driver not refused; the line is one line, starts with the pinned first sentence, names `OS_AUTH_SECRET` and the generator. The file also gains three module-top side-effect imports (`@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-settings`): `check:test-source-alias` asks every edited test file that reaches a lazy import in its source to pay the load during collection. Forced test edit, named here.
- `packages/cli/test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts`, new `describe` at the shipped entry (`bin/run.js` over `dist/`), no Redis needed because the door is in `os start`: (1) replicas declared over redis, no secret → exit 1, stderr carries the line, no `auth-secret` anywhere under home or cwd; (2) the secret set → the door passes (banner printed after it), nothing generated; (3) CONTROL replicas declared over `memory` → the secret is generated exactly as before (`.objectstack/auth-secret`). The single-node CONTROL is the file's existing leg 3, which reads the generated `auth-secret` file. Forced test edit, named here: `baseEnv` now also clears `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE`, `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS`, `OS_ALLOW_MEMORY_CLUSTER_MULTINODE` and `OS_REDIS_URL`, so an inherited declaration cannot reach the existing legs; the `test-budget` line is re-read (26.9 s, budget 40 unchanged).

## Acceptance notes

- **The refusal is in `os start` only.** A deployment that runs `os serve` directly already has to set `OS_AUTH_SECRET` (plugin-auth refuses production without it), so it never generated a per-replica secret.
- **With the image's durability switch on**, a start missing `OS_AUTH_SECRET` is refused by that check first (it lists every missing variable); this line is reached only without the switch or with the secret check passed.
- **The driver is read as written.** On open core with `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` > 1 and no multi-node gate registered, the `serve` child falls back to the memory driver and the split-brain guard refuses the boot anyway (measured on head with a shared secret set). That configuration now meets this line first when no secret is set; it never booted, so no boot is lost. `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` over redis did boot on base and is the narrowed path.
- **A deployment that already ran on generated secrets** keeps its sessions by setting `OS_AUTH_SECRET` to one replica's `auth-secret` contents on every replica; the changeset says so.

## Verification

Local, on head `c96d6e73` unless a line says otherwise. Every exit code below was captured before any pipe.

<details><summary>Step 0 and the real-Redis readings (redis-server 7.0.15, a probe app declaring the two cluster packages)</summary>

- Base `fc4c3072`, `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER=redis OS_REDIS_URL=… OS_SECRET_KEY=…`, no auth secret: `ClusterServicePlugin: registered "redis" driver`, `CacheServicePlugin: registered redis cache adapter`, `Press Ctrl+C to stop`; `{home}/.objectstack/auth-secret` generated.
- Head, the same environment: exit 1, the refusal line, 0 `auth-secret` files.
- Head, the same with `OS_AUTH_SECRET` set: redis driver and redis cache registered, `Press Ctrl+C to stop`, 0 `auth-secret` files.
- Two head replicas on one Redis and one shared SQLite file, one `OS_AUTH_SECRET`: a cookie signed in on r1 reads the session on r1 and on r2. The same pair with a different secret each (what base generated): r1 reads it, r2 does not.

</details>
